title: An empty stadium and even emptier commentary: RTÉ broadcasts Uefa feed of second Israel game
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
An empty stadium and even emptier commentary: RTÉ broadcasts Uefa feed of second Israel game

The national broadcaster curtailed its coverage for the two games.

Actual Article Body:

FOR THE SECOND successive Sunday, Ireland fans and otherwise curious viewers were treated to the bizarre spectacle of RTÉ’s compromise coverage of Ireland facing Israel in the Nations League.

The national broadcaster is curtailing how it covers the two games, and said last month that it would not be using its own employees on screen or studio punditry, with the commentary instead provided by Uefa’s global coverage.

RTÉ has said it is broadcasting the Uefa feed due to a decision to fulfil its “contractual obligations” while limiting commercial activity around the game. The broadcaster has been continuing to provide news coverage of the game and the events surrounding it.

No ads were broadcast before the match or at half-time.

As Ireland played their nominally home fixture against Israel in the north Serbian town of Bačka Topola tonight, things on TV looked much the same as they did last week.

The broadcast began with no introduction, continuity announcement, studio analysis or any of the other bells and whistles that would accompany an Ireland game aside from pictures and commentary from Uefa’s man on the ground.

The TV schedule said the game would start showing at 7.35pm, 10 minutes before kick-off, but the broadcaster so curtailed its coverage that it shaved another two minutes off the build-up and aired RTÉ 2′s staple Sunday evening nature documentary until 7.37pm.

After that belated introduction, much of the coverage from the Uefa feed was – like the notes in any good jazz standard – all about what the commentator didn’t say.

There has been no shortage of spikiness between the two sides in recent weeks, as well as questions about whether Ireland should play these games at all, whether the players would agree to do so, and why this game is happening 2,000km away from Dublin.

Tonight’s coverage did not allude to any of that, though there has been so much controversy around Ireland’s two fixtures against Israel that not even the Uefa guy could sanitise the elephant out of the room.

The pre-match patter began by referencing Israel’s game against Kosovo and Ireland’s 2-2 draw with Austria, with emphasis put on how a win here for either side would help them ahead of the final fixtures of the group.

It didn’t take long until the commentator made his first knowing reference to events off the pitch.

“Both these teams know the importance of a victory this evening in terms of…,” the commentator said, trailing off with a third-trimester pregnant pause before steering things back on course.

“… trying to avoid relegation from League B.”

To his credit, the man with the microphone didn’t completely shun the awkward reality around the game, but he certainly tried his hardest to avoid it.

Announcing the starting XIs, he observed that Ireland and Queens Park Rangers defender Jimmy Dunne has had “an interesting international break” after being named as a third-choice goalkeeper – though he didn’t explain when or why.

Uefa rules stipulate that international squads require three goalkeepers, and Dunne was nominated at short-notice alongside Caoimhín Kelleher and Max O’Leary after Gavin Bazunu decided to withdraw from the group ahead of last week’s fixture in Hungary.

Minutes later, the commentator noted that Bazunu had made himself unavailable for selection for this game, as he’d done last week, but again avoided enlightening viewers as to why this was the case.
